top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a distinct idea, the magic wavelength combined with Lamb-Dicke confinement, which lets thousands of neutral atoms be held with the trapping light shift cancelled; this differs from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It is mature and reproduced at several laboratories (about 1e-18 uncertainty, millimetre redshift, tighter bounds on constants and dark matter), and the allocation to Katori (proposal and first realisation) and Ye (record accuracy, many-body control) is unusually clean, provided the citation stays narrow and tied to the lattice clock. No award is clearly worse than awarding this.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; she is a theoretical atomic physicist working on atomic structure and precision calculations, with no documented connection to Katori or Ye, though she is a long-time collaborator of 2023 laureate L'Huillier
